messages:
eli (CSE): Heads-up — Helios support pinged us about repeated p99 spikes on their tenant (helios-prod) starting this morning ~08:00 UTC. They see p50~120ms, p95~360ms, but p99 jumps to 6–8s intermittently and a small bump in 500s. Customer is on shared hosted plan. :frowning: 

eli (CSE): Sample request IDs they attached: rq_01FZ6A2X9Y, rq_01FZ6B3Z2Q. They say it started after a big ingestion job on their side but it's hitting our /v1/completions endpoint and blocking user flows. They want a quick mitigation while we investigate.

sophie (eng-sre): @eli thanks — can you paste one full request payload (token lengths + model) and any stack traces or request IDs? Also is this short bursts or sustained? :eyes: 

eli (CSE): Pasted one sample (redacted):
```json
{
  "model": "open-redwood-large-v1",
  "input_tokens": 4100,
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "temperature": 0.2,
  "endpoint": "/v1/completions"
}
```
They said bursty — one large batch job runs every ~20m for ~2–3 minutes causing heavy tail.

sophie (eng-sre): Large input length + big max_tokens is immediate red flag — KV-cache pressure and long-generation slots. Could be noisy-neighboring their tenant hogging GPU workers and preventing smaller requests from getting scheduled.

Derek (eng-platform): Agreed. Quick mitigation options (fastest first):
- apply temporary per-tenant QPS cap / burst policy
- route helios-prod to a lower-batch dedicated pool (if capacity available)
- enforce endpoint-specific allowlist to prevent heavy batch job hitting completions directly

maria (prod-ops): I can push a temporary rate limit now. Proposed: 30 rps steady, burst 150 for 1 hour while we validate. Command: 
```bash
rwctl tenant update --tenant helios-prod --rate-limit "30rps" --burst 150 --expires "1h"
```
Please confirm before I run.

eli (CSE): Please push it, customer agreed to temporary throttle. They prefer routing while they refactor.

maria (prod-ops): Running now... :hammer_and_wrench:
(maria (prod-ops) added reaction :thumbsup:)

ops-bot: rate-limit-update: tenant=helios-prod applied rate=30rps burst=150 expires=2026-03-15T10:12:34Z actor=maria

sophie (eng-sre): While ops did that, I'll check worker queues and KV cache eviction rates. Can you share link to traces for rq_01FZ6A2X9Y? Need span timing for scheduling vs generation.

eli (CSE): Trace links: https://traces.internal/trace/rq_01FZ6A2X9Y and https://traces.internal/trace/rq_01FZ6B3Z2Q. Customer also sent a flame: 80% time in 'wait-for-batching' and 'kernel-run' spans.

sophie (eng-sre): Looking — the traces show long queue wait ~4.9s and kernel-run ~1.2s for the big requests. Queue wait correlates with high batch sizes being built because multiple long-gen requests are backlogged. Also seeing frequent KV cache evictions on those workers: eviction rate spiking at the same timestamps.

derek (eng-platform): That matches noisy neighbor hypothesis. Short-term: throttling should reduce queue wait for others. Medium-term: we should add per-tenant prioritized scheduling and an allowlist to limit heavy-generation from non-API paths. Long-term: traffic shaping + tenant-level preemption or dedicated lanes.

maria (prod-ops): I pushed an endpoint-level allowlist to block large-batch submissions from their ingestion job to completions. Command used: 
```bash
rwctl allowlist add --tenant helios-prod --endpoint "/v1/completions" --max-input-tokens 2000 --note "temp block for background ingestion"
```
Helios agreed to back off their ingestion for now.

eli (CSE): Customer just confirmed after throttle+allowlist: p99 dropped to ~420ms, error rate normalized. They said their ingestion jobs will be reconfigured. :tada: 

sophie (eng-sre): Nice work. I'll open a postmortem/retro and add the traces + eviction graphs. Action items:
- create infra ticket for tenant-level scheduling (ENG-4721)
- add an alert rule for tenant p99 delta > 1s vs baseline (MON-ops)
- add automated suggested limits for large-token requests in docs/SDK (devex)

derek (eng-platform): Also recommend we add an operator runbook: when a tenant causes queue wait > 2s for >5min, auto-apply gentle throttles and notify CSE + tenant. I'll draft it.

maria (prod-ops): Filed short-term JIRA for temporary policies and put in a roll window for this weekend to test per-tenant lanes. Ticket: OPS-3132.

eli (CSE): Customer is happy with the temporary fix and wants a follow-up call tomorrow to review traffic shaping options.

sophie (eng-sre): I'll collate traces + the eviction metrics and post link to the retrospective doc in #postmortems in an hour.

eli (CSE): Thanks team — closing the immediate escalation. Marking as resolved with notes sent to Helios. :white_check_mark: 

maria (prod-ops): Leaving the temporary rate-limit until 10:12 UTC, will auto-expire. If we want to extend, comment here.

eli (CSE): If we do long-term lanes, pls include cost estimates and perf SLOs for dedicated pool vs tenant-lane.

sophie (eng-sre): noted. tagging ENG + PLG for prioritization.

(maria (prod-ops) added reaction :spiral_calendar_pad:)
